chains.name: Ethereum
chains.detail: EF Protocol cluster target (Sep 7 2026): Ethereum L1 quantum-resistant across execution, consensus and data by December 2029, held as non-negotiable until a January 2027 reassessment; plans for Q-day as early as 2030 and calls that assumption deliberately aggressive. A minimum-viable PQ fallback (PQ public-key registry, PQ consensus heartbeat, leanDA sampling, leanSPHINCS transactions) sits at fork J* per the Aug 19 2026 Strawmap update. Dedicated PQ team since Jan 2026. Hash-based validator signatures (leanSig) run on devnets only; nothing PQ is on mainnet. Design still contested: on Oct 19 2026 Vitalik backed EIP-8288 and argued no new precompiles are needed, against the roadmap's precompile milestone. EIP-7702 delegation does not remove the original key's control of an account.
chains.exposure: Every account that has ever sent a transaction exposes its public key. The top 1,000 such accounts hold ~20.5M ETH (Google, Mar 2026). ~37M staked ETH relies on BLS signing keys (consensus risk); stake withdrawals go to ordinary ECDSA addresses.
watch: Glamsterdam ships on schedule (Dec 2026) — first test of the 7–9 month fork cadence the 2029 target needs
January 2027 reassessment keeps or moves the December 2029 target
EIP-8288 vs precompile dispute resolved in the Strawmap
PQ key registry (fork I*) reaches a public testnet
Wallets let users register a PQ key for an existing account

migration_target.basis: EF Protocol cluster target for full PQ readiness (execution, consensus, data)

checkpoints.label: Glamsterdam ships on mainnet (fork-cadence test)
checkpoints.evidence: Targeted for December 2026; the 2029 plan needs an average 7.2-month cadence through five more forks.

checkpoints.label: January 2027 reassessment keeps the December 2029 target
checkpoints.evidence: EF treats the date as non-negotiable until this review with outside experts.

checkpoints.label: Minimum-viable PQ (fork J*) live on mainnet
checkpoints.evidence: Contingency milestone reachable on a 12-month cadence from Glamsterdam.

checkpoints.label: Full PQ readiness across all three layers
checkpoints.evidence: Requires roughly a 9-month cadence to fork K*.

governance_flags.label: Design dispute
governance_flags.detail: Vitalik's Oct 19 2026 support for EIP-8288 (no new precompiles) contradicts the roadmap's precompile milestone.

governance_flags.label: Fork cadence
governance_flags.detail: Linear fork shipping cannot meet the 2029 date by the EF's own math; it needs parallel fork work and more contributors.

governance_flags.label: Dormant-ETH policy
governance_flags.detail: No freeze proposal on the table. Precedent cuts both ways: the Parity-recovery EIP-999 was withdrawn.

chains.name: Bitcoin
chains.detail: BIP-360 (P2MR, Pay-to-Merkle-Root — Taproot without the key-path spend; formerly P2QRH) merged as a draft Feb 2026; no activation plan or date. BIP-361 (Lopp et al., legacy-signature sunset/freeze) is a draft. Hash-based address types (P2PKH/P2WPKH) protect unspent outputs until first spend; Taproot (P2TR) outputs expose the key on-chain. Oct 2026: Justin Drake's 'bunker mode' call urges migrating exposed-key funds to fresh hash-protected addresses. Oct 13 2026: Coinbase (custodian of ~5% of BTC) published recommendations, framed as 'input to an open discussion' — start now, P2MR/P2TRv2 output containers, a staged 1-of-2 hybrid (classical or PQ key) spend path, a stateless PQ option, MPC-friendly schemes for custodians; dormant-coin policy handled separately, no position taken. Oct 15 2026: Google demonstrated magic state cultivation on hardware. Google's March 2026 ECDLP-256 estimate depends on cultivation and concludes that on fast-clock machines on-spend (mempool) attacks arrive at essentially the same time as at-rest attacks — so hash-protected outputs are exposed at first spend, and the exposed-key total is a floor, not a ceiling.
chains.exposure: ~6-6.9M BTC (~31% of supply) behind exposed public keys — reused addresses, spent-from addresses, P2PK, and Taproot (CoinDesk, Europol, Oct 2026)
watch: Coinbase's 1-of-2 hybrid spend path appears in a BIP or Bitcoin Core PR
A PQ signature BIP (e.g. SHRINCS) selects an MPC-compatible scheme custodians can run
Coinbase or ETF sponsors publish a dated custody-key migration plan

migration_target.basis: No activation plan. BIP-361 Phase A would start ~3 years (160,000 blocks) after an activation that has no date.

checkpoints.label: A PQ signature scheme gets a BIP number (e.g. SHRINCS)
checkpoints.evidence: SHRINCS draft published by Blockstream Aug 27 2026; hash-based, ~324–580 byte signatures; no BIP number or completed security proof.

checkpoints.label: P2MR (BIP-360) merged into Bitcoin Core with activation parameters
checkpoints.evidence: BIP-360 merged as Draft Feb 11 2026; no Core PR with activation parameters and no miner signaling.

checkpoints.label: Rough consensus on dormant-coin (freeze) policy
checkpoints.evidence: BIP-361 (Lopp et al.) proposes a staged sunset; Adam Back opposes a forced freeze; Coinbase wants the question handled separately.

checkpoints.label: Major hardware wallets ship PQ output support

governance_flags.label: Freeze-or-not dispute
governance_flags.detail: The main blocker is whether to freeze unmigrated coins, not the cryptography. No resolution path yet.

governance_flags.label: Funding
governance_flags.detail: Bitcoin Security Consortium (BlackRock, Fidelity, Coinbase and others) pledged $15M over three years in Jul 2026.

governance_flags.label: Chain-split threat
governance_flags.detail: No competing client or fork announced over the quantum question.

projection.basis: Best case for Bitcoin: a PQ soft fork activates within 1 year of today, faster than Taproot (~22 months from BIP publication to activation). Network-level protection then follows BIP-361: Phase A at ~3 years, Phase B (legacy spends locked behind a rescue protocol) 2 years later.

chains.name: Algorand
chains.detail: State proofs use Falcon (NIST PQC finalist). Partial PQC integration.
chains.exposure: Partial — state proofs are PQ-secure, transaction sigs are not
watch: Full transaction signature migration to PQC
